subject: Community Preservation Act Overview
overview: Roberta Cameron, Chair of the Community Preservation Committee, discussed the impact and administration of the Community Preservation Act (CPA) in Medford. The conversation detailed how tax surcharges fund local projects in housing, historic preservation, and recreation, emphasizing community-led planning and equity.

items.title: CPA Funding Mechanism and Purpose
items.summary: The CPA is funded by a 1.5% property tax surcharge and state matches, generating approximately $2 million annually for open space, outdoor recreation, historic preservation, and affordable housing.

items.title: Project Selection and Approval Process
items.summary: A nine-member Community Preservation Committee evaluates grant applications from city departments and community partners before making funding recommendations to the City Council for final approval.

items.title: Local Impact and Project Highlights
items.summary: The program has funded 90 projects totaling $10 million over five years, including Chevalier Theatre renovations, COVID-19 emergency rental assistance, and the redevelopment of the Walkling Court housing site.

items.title: Advancing Equity Through Community Engagement
items.summary: The committee prioritizes inclusive recruitment and requires public visioning processes for major capital improvements, such as the redesign of the McGlynn School playground into an inclusive facility.

items.title: Public Access and Five-Year Celebration
items.summary: The committee plans to hold a public event celebrating five years of CPA work and maintains a map of all funded projects on their dedicated website.
